chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Playing the feature tune in Shaft's second film
summary: Gordon Parks insisted on Royal for a ballad in the second Shaft film, recorded in one rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: That's very interesting to know. I remember a film that I wanted to mention, because (inaudible)

few years ago, that was (inaudible), because Gordon Parks told me at the screening ________, to him, Marshal Royal, he said, "I told him 'I got to have Marshal Royal'." He said, "Doesn't that sound beautiful?" He said that when he -- I guess he wrote ________ lines for things and then (inaudible).
That was the second series of Shaft. That was the second one.
Yeah, the first one was done by --
Yeah, that -- I don't know who it was done by, but I worked on the second one.
I did some of the recording for the second Shaft. I did the feature tune of the thing. It's a ballad type thing and I played it.
I think that's the name of it. That's it.

Yeah, yeah. ________ Smith made a recording of it, I believe. He's the one who did the vocal, ________ Smith. I thought it was a very good tune. I would have loved to have done it as a single on an album, because it was a very good tune and I liked it very much. I only played it the one time we rehearsed it. We ran it down one
time, to see if the notes were all correct on it and then we cut it and I have never played it before or since.
It was so beautiful, what you did.
I thought it was very nice.
It was exactly what Gordon had in mind, he said, when he specified he had to have you.
I'm very glad that he did.
A little showcasing never harms anyone once in a while.
